newsitem.title: UK: June Brent closes seven cents down but off lows.
newsitem.headline: June Brent closes seven cents down but off lows.

text.p: IPE June Brent closed at seven cents lower at $19.55 a barrel on Wednesday, off the day's lows, after briefly breaking to higher ground in last minute trading, brokers said.

They said that IPE followed NYMEX's lead as the U.S. market seemed to have shrgged off bearish U.S. weekly stock figures that showed a rise in both crude and gasoline stocks in the United States last week.

"After being absolutely comatose, the market suddenly turned around and moved upwards, into fresh high ground for the day. I can't find any particular fundamental reason for it,," one broker said minutes before June Brent rose as high as $19.65, or three cents higher than Tuesday's close, as Wednesday's session neared its end.
But in the last few minutes, the contract dipped again, to close lower, but way away from earlier lows.

IPE Brent, which expires on Thursday, hit a low of $19.20, or 42 cents a barrel below Tuesday's close, earlier in the day as the U.S. data which showed a rise in both crude and gasoline stocks last week in the United States was still fresh.

In the afternoon the contract shed some of its earlier losses to trade around the $19.35 mark as IPE traders said they were following NYMEX's lead and sensed that the U.S. market may well have decided to ignore the weekly inventory figures.
"It seems to have done so," said one IPE broker when asked if the bearish data was not being strongly taken into consideration.
NYMEX's WTI June closed one cent down at $21.36 after being called to open some 50 cents down.
The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) data on Wednesday showed that crude stocks rose 6.4 million barrels and gasoline stocks were up 4.7 million barrels last week.

The DOE data confirmed American Petroleum Institute (API) figures issued late on Tuesday which said U.S. crude stocks rose 6.94 million barrels and gasoline stocks grew by 6.51 million barrels last week.
Earlier, IPE June gas oil closed $2.50 down at $170.75 a tonne, but off the day's lows, pushed down by the U.S. stock reports, traders said.
The contract traded as high as $171.75 but also as low as $169.75 soon after NYMEX opened lower following the release of the DOE data.
